title: Castle Bravo Nuclear Test and the Daigo Fukuryu Maru Incident
summary: On 1 March 1954, the United States detonated Castle Bravo at Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands, producing a 15-megaton yield that exceeded theoretical predictions by more than twofold. Dangerous radioactive fallout contaminated hundreds of Marshallese residents on Rongelap and Utirik Atolls, American servicemen, and the crew of the Japanese tuna trawler Daigo Fukuryu Maru (Lucky Dragon No. 5). The resulting radiation sickness and death provoked fierce international outrage, catalyzing Japan's Gensuikyo ban-the-bomb movement and accelerating global mobilization against nuclear testing.

where.historical_name: Bikini Atoll, Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands

importance.justification: Castle Bravo was the highest-yield thermonuclear test in United States history, producing widespread radiological fallout that poisoned Indigenous populations and Japanese fishermen and sparked the global anti-nuclear testing movement.

audience_note: Details severe radiation poisoning, radioactive fallout contamination, acute radiation syndrome, and long-term health crises among exposed populations.
